The loading guard is cleared when the catalogue arrives, before its StoreKit request completes. A screen visit can therefore start another discovery while the first product request is in flight. Responses are applied without checking which catalogue produced them, so a late, partial response can replace newer products and leave plans missing or joined against the wrong catalogue.

findings.claim: Catalogue and StoreKit failures report an error without clearing the prior plan options or StoreKit products. After a successful discovery, a later failed refresh can thus leave old plans and their purchase buttons available even though current availability and catalogue terms could not be verified.

findings.claim: The decoder accepts multiple entries with the same nonempty key. If the backend supplies two such plans with different products, selecting the second row stores that shared key, but purchase lookup resolves the first matching option. findings.claim: The TLS vhost now proxies to a plain HTTP FPM listener and sets only forwarded headers. WordPress normally determines HTTPS from the server HTTPS or port variables, not X-Forwarded-Proto, so this can cause admin redirect loops and incorrect secure URL or cookie behavior. An existing application-level proxy override could prevent the regression, but it is not established by these configurations.
findings.note: Terra-exclusive: TLS-terminating vhost proxies to plain-HTTP FPM, sets X-Forwarded-Proto only; no wp-config HTTPS fixup in scope, so WordPress is_ssl() false (canonical/http downgrade, non-Secure cookies). New vhost at head. 2/3.

findings.claim: The new readiness check requires status to match the provider URL, model and key-variable name. The CLI records the raw test result, which omits model and api_key_env, so successfully tested providers with either field set remain unready and web submission returns 409.
findings.note: New 3-tuple readiness gate (url,model,key) vs pre-existing CLI raw record_test (stores identity (url,'','')): CLI-tested endpoints with model/key configured can never show Ready. New gate created the inconsistency. 3/3.

findings.claim: An environment-resolved ASR URL is marked Ready without a probe. The default Compose service sets that URL even though the ASR container is behind an optional profile, so a normal deployment without that profile can queue transcription jobs that cannot reach the server.

findings.claim: Session validation checks only the stored token and expiry, not the password under which the session was created. Changing the operator password and restarting therefore leaves previously issued sessions authorized until logout or the 14-day expiry.
findings.note: New auth.py session validation binds token+expiry only; password change/rotation does not invalidate sessions. Moderate session-management gap. 3/3.

findings.claim: Save-and-test writes the endpoint before testing it, while the browser reports 'Not saved' when the test fails. Editing an assigned provider to an unreachable URL can thus replace its working configuration and invalidate its qualification even though the operator is told it was not saved.
findings.note: save-test persists config via save_one before probing; on test failure UI says 'Not saved' while the failed endpoint is already the active config. 1/3 app.py wording.

findings.claim: After a probe completes, record_qualified overwrites its tested identity with the provider currently saved under that name. If another request changes that provider during the probe, the first result can be recorded against and assign roles to the untested replacement.
findings.note: record_qualified replaces the tested result identity (rep1 wording).

findings.claim: The source reprocess route calls enqueue without caption information, unlike job reprocessing, which passes the prior job's caption flag. Consequently, with no ASR configured, source reprocessing rejects a caption-backed job even when job reprocessing can accept it.
findings.note: Source-reprocess enqueue drops has_captions while job-retry path passes it: reprocessed sources lose manual-caption subtitles. Minor. 2/3.

findings.claim: The CLI records test_endpoint's result without adding the configured model and API-key variable. For providers using either field, provider_status now rejects that successful result as an identity mismatch, so the documented CLI save-and-test workflow leaves writing or transcription unready and web jobs blocked.
findings.note: Same CLI/gate inconsistency (rep2 wording).

findings.claim: When an endpoint exposes exactly one model and the model field was blank, Test fills that field after recording a result bound to the blank model. Saving then prunes the mismatched result, so the UI's advertised test-then-save sequence leaves the endpoint unqualified until it is tested again.
findings.note: Single-model autofill without persist; same behavior at base (modulo message). Trivial UX quirk. 1/3.

findings.claim: record_qualified replaces the tested identity with the provider currently stored under the name. If another request changes that provider while the network test is in flight, the first test's success is recorded against the new URL, model and key and can assign roles to an endpoint that was never tested.
findings.note: Same identity-overwrite defect (rep2 wording; race made explicit).

findings.claim: An ASR URL from the environment is marked Ready without a probe. The default Compose service always sets http://asr:9000 while the ASR container is enabled only by an optional profile, so a normal deployment without that profile can queue transcription-dependent jobs against a nonexistent service.
findings.note: Env ASR Ready w/o probe (reps 1-2 wording).

findings.claim: Session validation checks only the token and expiry, not the password or a credential generation. After an operator changes the configured password and restarts, previously issued cookies remain authorized until logout or their 14-day expiry, preventing password rotation from revoking compromised sessions.
findings.note: New auth.py session validation binds token+expiry only; password change/rotation does not invalidate sessions. Moderate session-management gap. 3/3.

findings.claim: The documented Caddy example terminates TLS and proxies over HTTP, so request.url.scheme is HTTP and the operator cookie lacks Secure unless YT2WIKI_COOKIE_SECURE=1 is explicitly set. The deployment instructions do not mention that setting, leaving the session cookie eligible for transmission over HTTP on the same host.
findings.note: Scheme-dependent Secure-cookie flag (request.url.scheme) behind documented TLS-terminating Caddy example with no fixup instruction: session cookies issued without Secure in the documented deployment. Low-moderate. 1/3 app.py wording.

findings.claim: The new readiness check runs only in enqueue, after the uploaded video has been copied into canonical storage and its source created. A 409 for an unready writer or ASR therefore leaves a stored video and source without a job; repeated rejected uploads can consume substantial disk space.
findings.note: Same readiness-ordering defect (rep2 wording). Merged: one distinct defect in 2/3 reps.

findings.claim: Sessions are validated only by token and expiry, not against the current password. Changing the operator password and restarting therefore leaves previously issued cookies authorized for up to 14 days, including a session whose password or cookie was compromised.
findings.note: New auth.py session validation binds token+expiry only; password change/rotation does not invalidate sessions. Moderate session-management gap. 3/3.

findings.claim: The documented reverse proxy terminates TLS before forwarding HTTP to the app, but does not instruct operators to set YT2WIKI_COOKIE_SECURE=1. In that configuration the app sees an HTTP scheme and issues a cookie without Secure, allowing it to be sent over HTTP to the same host.
findings.note: Same scheme/Secure-cookie defect, docs-side wording (rep3). Merged: one distinct defect in 2/3 reps.

findings.claim: The new readiness check requires status to contain the provider's URL, model and API-key variable. Existing status records with the same shape are also affected.

findings.claim: Any nonempty environment ASR URL is reported Ready without a reachability or protocol test. The default Compose configuration always sets http://asr:9000 but starts that service only with the optional asr profile. Consequently the readiness gate accepts uploads and uncaptioned videos that then fail transcription on a default deployment.
findings.note: Env-resolved ASR URL marked Ready with no reachability probe while default Compose always sets YT2WIKI_ASR_URL (service profile-gated off): gate vacuous for default deployments; jobs queue against a non-existent service. Historical P15-5 concern class, reintroduced by the new gate. 3/3.

findings.claim: After probing an endpoint, record_qualified reloads the current provider and overwrites the tested result's identity with it. If another request changes the same provider during the probe, a pass for the old URL or model is attributed to the new one and roles are assigned to an untested endpoint.

findings.claim: The readiness check now occurs inside enqueue, after the entire upload has been copied and registered as a source. When readiness returns 409, the canonical upload and source remain despite no job being created; repeated attempts with different videos can fill the persistent volume.
findings.note: Readiness gate executes inside enqueue after upload copied and source registered: doomed uploads stored before rejection (orphaned rows, wasted copy). Ordering inefficiency; minor. 2/3.

findings.claim: New URL submissions pass their manual-caption status to enqueue, and job reprocessing carries that status forward, but source reprocessing calls enqueue without it. A captioned source that can be submitted without ASR is therefore rejected by the equivalent source-reprocess API when ASR is not ready.
findings.note: Source-reprocess enqueue drops has_captions while job-retry path passes it: reprocessed sources lose manual-caption subtitles. Minor. 2/3.

findings.claim: The UI tells the operator an unreachable endpoint was not saved, but save-test writes the provider before probing it. Editing an existing provider to an unreachable URL therefore replaces the working configuration and invalidates its qualification despite the failure message.
findings.note: Same save-test defect, UI-side wording (rep3). Merged with the app.py instance: one distinct defect in 2/3 reps.
